author.name: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
author.occupation: German political writers and revolutionary socialists
author.biography: Marx's journalism brought conflict with authorities and years of exile. Engels came from a manufacturing family and saw industrial Manchester at close quarters. Their partnership joined philosophical argument to the world of factories, wages and ownership. Written for the Communist League on the eve of the upheavals of 1848, this short book turns their account of modern society into a direct appeal to the people they believed could overturn it.

hook.text: How free are you when someone else controls your livelihood?

paragraphs: The modern economy can transform the world while leaving many of the people doing the work with little control over their lives. Marx and Engels make that tension the beginning of a call for political action.

The Manifesto is short, combative and designed to recruit. It presents capitalism as an astonishingly productive system whose achievements also create instability and conflict. Class becomes a way of reading relations that may otherwise appear private, voluntary or simply inevitable.

Its compression gives the prose force and leaves large questions open. Readers should distinguish its historical claims, predictions and political demands rather than treating agreement with one as agreement with all. The later history of movements invoking it does not remove the need to examine what the text actually says.
Read with attention to who can bargain and who must accept the available terms. When does a formally free choice conceal a very unequal distribution of power?

orientation.text: This is a political manifesto, not a complete presentation of Marx's economics. Separate its account of history from its immediate programme and later uses.
